citation: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass
paraphrase: Jesus declares that until the current heavens and earth disappear, not the smallest letter or stroke will be removed from the Law until everything is accomplished.
contexte: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus affirms that He has come not to abolish the Law or the Prophets but to fulfill them.

citation: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly declares that no one born of a woman has arisen greater than John the Baptist, yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to the crowds about John the Baptist, after asking what they went out to see and declaring John to be more than a prophet.

citation: Of a truth thou art the Son of God.
paraphrase: Those in the boat worshipped Jesus, acknowledging that He is truly the Son of God.
contexte: After Jesus saved Peter from sinking and calmed the storm, those in the boat worshipped Him.

citation: Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.
paraphrase: Jesus affirms that Elias will indeed come first to restore all things, yet also declares that Elias has already come unrecognized and suffered, which the disciples understood as John the Baptist.
contexte: After descending the mountain, Jesus' disciples ask why the scribes say Elias must come first, prompting his reply about Elias and his coming.

citation: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.
paraphrase: Jesus tells his disciples that it is very difficult for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
contexte: After the rich young man departed sorrowful because he had great possessions, Jesus turns to his disciples to teach about the difficulty of the rich entering the kingdom of heaven.

citation: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
paraphrase: Jesus asks which of the two sons did the father's will; they answer the first, and Jesus tells them that the publicans and harlots enter God's kingdom before them.
contexte: After the parable of the two sons, Jesus asks the chief priests and elders which son did the father's will, and they answer the first.

citation: we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth
paraphrase: They sent their disciples with the Herodians to say to Jesus, 'Teacher, we know you are truthful and teach God's way truthfully, and you don't care about anyone's opinion, for you don't show partiality.'
contexte: The Pharisees, seeking to entangle Jesus, send their disciples along with the Herodians to question him.

citation: Verily I say unto you, I know you not.
paraphrase: The bridegroom answers the late virgins, solemnly declaring that he does not recognize them as his own.
contexte: The foolish virgins arrive late to the marriage and ask the bridegroom to open the door, but he replies that he does not know them.

citation: Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
paraphrase: During the meal, Jesus truthfully tells his disciples that one of them will betray him.
contexte: Jesus is eating the Passover meal with his twelve disciples.

citation: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly declares that every sin and blasphemy committed by people can be forgiven.
contexte: Jesus responds to scribes who accused him of casting out demons by Beelzebub, after warning that a divided Satan cannot stand and that one must bind the strong man before spoiling his house.

citation: and told him all the truth
paraphrase: The woman, afraid and trembling because she knew she had been healed, came and bowed before Jesus and honestly told him everything that had happened.
contexte: Jesus has just healed a woman with an issue of blood, and she approaches him in fear and trembling after realizing she cannot hide what happened.

citation: Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly declares that no one can enter God's kingdom unless they receive it with the humble, trusting attitude of a little child.
contexte: After the disciples rebuked those bringing children to Jesus, He welcomed them and used a child's receptivity to teach about entering God's kingdom.

citation: we know that thou art true, and carest for no man
paraphrase: They address Jesus as a truthful teacher who shows no partiality and teaches God's way truthfully, then ask whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar.
contexte: The Pharisees and Herodians are sent to catch Jesus in his words, flattering him before asking about paying tribute to Caesar.

citation: Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God
paraphrase: The scribe tells Jesus that He has spoken truth, affirming that there is only one God and no other.
contexte: A scribe questions Jesus about the greatest commandment, and after Jesus answers, the scribe agrees with His teaching.

citation: And as they sat and did eat, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.
paraphrase: Jesus solemnly declares that one of his own disciples, who is sharing the meal with him, will betray him.
contexte: During the Last Supper, as Jesus and his disciples were eating, he reveals that one of them will betray him.

citation: Truly this man was the Son of God.
paraphrase: When the centurion who stood facing Jesus saw how he cried out and breathed his last, he declared that Jesus was truly the Son of God.
contexte: After Jesus cried out and died, the centurion standing nearby witnessed the manner of his death and made a declaration.

citation: who will commit to your trust the true riches?
paraphrase: If you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
contexte: Jesus teaches his disciples about faithfulness with wealth, contrasting unrighteous mammon with true riches.

citation: but teachest the way of God truly:
paraphrase: They asked Jesus, calling him Teacher, acknowledging that he speaks and teaches correctly and shows no partiality, but teaches God's way truthfully.
auteur: Spies (sent by the chief priests and scribes)
contexte: The chief priests and scribes sent spies who pretended to be sincere in order to trap Jesus in his words.

citation: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
paraphrase: Jesus observes that the poor widow has given more than all the rich donors, because she gave all she had to live on.
contexte: Jesus watches rich men and a poor widow putting gifts into the treasury, and he comments on the widow's offering.

citation: Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.
paraphrase: About an hour later, another person strongly asserted that Peter was truly with Jesus because Peter was a Galilean.
contexte: After Peter twice denied knowing Jesus, a third person insists about an hour later that Peter was with Jesus, prompting Peter’s third denial just before the rooster crows.

citation: Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
paraphrase: Jesus assures the repentant thief that he will be with him in paradise that very day.
contexte: While being crucified between two thieves, one of them asks Jesus to remember him when he comes into his kingdom.

citation: Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;
paraphrase: Some women among our group amazed us by going to the tomb early in the morning.
auteur: Cleopas (disciple on the road to Emmaus)
contexte: Two disciples, walking to Emmaus after the crucifixion, recount to the risen Jesus how women from their group had astonished them by finding the tomb empty.

citation: That was the true Light, which lighteth every man
paraphrase: The Light, which is the Word, is the genuine light that illuminates every person entering the world.
contexte: John the Baptist testified about the Light so that all might believe, but he himself was not that Light.

citation: full of grace and truth.
paraphrase: The Word became human and lived among us, and we saw his glory, the glory of the Father's only Son, full of grace and truth.
contexte: After declaring that believers become children of God, the apostle John affirms that the Word became flesh and lived among us, revealing the Father's glory.

citation: but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ
paraphrase: The law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
contexte: John the Baptist testifies about Jesus, and the narrator explains that while the law was given through Moses, grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

citation: Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
paraphrase: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, he remarked that Nathanael was a true Israelite without deceit.
contexte: Jesus sees Nathanael coming toward him after Philip had invited him, and he makes a statement about Nathanael's character.

citation: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open
paraphrase: Jesus tells Nathanael that he will see heaven opened and angels ascending and descending on the Son of man, affirming the truth of this future revelation.
contexte: Jesus responds to Nathanael's confession of faith after being amazed that Jesus saw him under the fig tree.

citation: We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen
paraphrase: Jesus tells Nicodemus that he and his witnesses speak what they know and testify to what they have seen, yet Nicodemus and his peers do not accept their testimony.
contexte: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and teacher of Israel, questions how the new birth Jesus described is possible, and Jesus responds by contrasting divine testimony with human unbelief.

citation: But he that doeth truth cometh to the light
paraphrase: But whoever practices truth comes to the light, so that it may be clear that their deeds are done in God.
contexte: Jesus is explaining to Nicodemus that people are condemned for loving darkness rather than light, while those who do truth come to the light.

citation: hath set to his seal that God is true.
paraphrase: Whoever accepts Jesus's testimony confirms by that act that God is truthful.
contexte: John the Baptist explains that Jesus, who comes from above and speaks what he has seen and heard, is affirmed as true by those who receive his testimony, while others reject it.

citation: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.
paraphrase: Jesus tells the woman that she has had five husbands and the man she is currently with is not her husband, confirming that she spoke truthfully.
contexte: Jesus is speaking with a Samaritan woman at a well, and after she admits she has no husband, he reveals his knowledge of her past and present marital situation.

citation: the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth
paraphrase: The time is coming and is already here when genuine worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such people to worship Him.
contexte: Jesus is speaking with a Samaritan woman at a well, explaining that true worship is not tied to a specific location but is a matter of spirit and truth.

citation: they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth
paraphrase: God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and in truth.
contexte: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman at a well, teaching her about true worship in contrast to the worship of the Samaritans and Jews.

citation: And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples about the spiritual harvest, using the proverb of sowing and reaping to illustrate how they will reap where others have labored.

citation: we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ
paraphrase: The Samaritans tell the woman that they now believe, not because of her report, but because they have heard Jesus themselves and know that He is truly the Christ, the Savior of the world.
contexte: After Jesus stayed two days with the Samaritans, many believed because of His own word, and they told the woman that their faith now rested on firsthand hearing.

citation: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
contexte: Jesus is defending the validity of his testimony before those who question his authority, explaining that he does not act or judge on his own authority but seeks the Father's will.

citation: There is another that beareth witness of me
paraphrase: Another testifies about me, and I know that his testimony about me is true.
contexte: Jesus is defending the validity of His testimony, explaining that He does not bear witness of Himself but relies on another witness whom He knows to be true.

citation: he bare witness unto the truth
paraphrase: Jesus reminds his hearers that they themselves sent messengers to John the Baptist, and John testified truthfully about him.
contexte: Jesus is answering his accusers about the validity of his testimony, pointing to John the Baptist as a witness they themselves consulted.

citation: This is of a truth that prophet that should come into the world.
paraphrase: Voyant le miracle que Jésus avait accompli, les hommes dirent qu'il était vraiment le prophète attendu qui devait venir dans le monde.
contexte: Après que Jésus a nourri cinq mille personnes avec cinq pains d'orge et deux poissons, les gens qui avaient été rassasiés ont reconnu le miracle.

citation: but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
paraphrase: Jesus tells the crowd that Moses did not give them the bread from heaven; rather, it is his Father who gives them the true bread from heaven.
contexte: The crowd asks Jesus for a sign like the manna their fathers ate in the desert, prompting him to correct their understanding of the true bread from heaven.

citation: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to the crowd in the synagogue at Capernaum, explaining the necessity of eating his flesh and drinking his blood to have eternal life.

citation: the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him
paraphrase: Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory, but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truthful and without unrighteousness.
contexte: Jesus is defending his teaching before the crowd, claiming it comes from God who sent him.

citation: but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not
paraphrase: Jesus declares that his Father who sent him is true, though the people do not know him.
contexte: Jesus teaches in the temple during the Feast of Tabernacles, responding to the crowd's debate about whether he is the Christ and their claims to know his origins.

citation: Of a truth this is the Prophet.
paraphrase: After hearing Jesus' teaching, many in the crowd declared that Jesus was truly the Prophet.
contexte: After Jesus spoke of rivers of living water, the crowd debated his identity, with some acknowledging him as the Prophet.

citation: thy record is not true
paraphrase: The Pharisees accused Jesus of bearing witness about Himself, claiming that such self-testimony is not true.
contexte: After Jesus declared Himself the light of the world, the Pharisees challenged His testimony as self-serving and therefore untrue.

citation: Jesus answered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye cannot tell whence I come, and whither I go.
paraphrase: Jesus defends his testimony as true despite bearing witness of himself, because he knows his divine origin and destination, while his critics do not.
contexte: After the Pharisees challenged Jesus' self-testimony as false, Jesus responds by asserting the truth of his witness.

citation: And yet if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.
paraphrase: Jesus asserts that even when he does judge, his judgment is true, because he is not alone but is with the Father who sent him.
contexte: Jesus responds to the Pharisees who challenged his testimony, asserting that his judgment is true because he is not alone but with the Father who sent him.

citation: the testimony of two men is true.
paraphrase: The law states that the testimony of two men is true.
contexte: Jesus is defending the truth of his testimony before the Pharisees, appealing to their law about witnesses.

citation: I have many things to say and to judge of you: but he that sent me is true; and I speak to the world those things which I have heard of him.
paraphrase: Jesus tells his opponents that he has much to say and judge about them, yet the one who sent him is true, and he speaks to the world only what he has heard from him.
contexte: Jesus responds to the Pharisees' question about his identity, affirming that his testimony comes from the Father who sent him.

citation: If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed;
paraphrase: Jesus tells the Jews who believed in him that if they remain faithful to his teaching, they are truly his disciples.
contexte: After many believed on him as he spoke, Jesus addresses those Jews who believed, teaching about true discipleship.

citation: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to Jews who had believed in him, urging them to continue in his word as true disciples.

citation: a man that hath told you the truth, which I have heard of God
paraphrase: Jesus confronts his opponents, pointing out that they are trying to kill him even though he has spoken the truth he received from God, unlike Abraham.
contexte: Jesus is responding to those who claim Abraham as their father, contrasting their murderous intent with Abraham's faithfulness.

citation: abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him
paraphrase: Jesus tells his opponents that they belong to the devil, whose desires they follow; the devil was a murderer from the beginning and did not remain in the truth, because there is no truth in him—when he lies, he speaks from his own nature, for he is a liar and the father of lies.
contexte: Jesus addresses hostile listeners, contrasting their true spiritual father with God and explaining why they reject his word.

citation: And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not.
contexte: Jesus confronts his unbelieving audience, contrasting their resistance to truth with their father the devil, who is a liar.

citation: And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?
paraphrase: No one can convict Jesus of sin, yet his truthful words are rejected by those who refuse to believe.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to the Jews who have just called him a Samaritan and accused him of having a devil, after he exposed their father the devil as the source of lies.

citation: all things that John spake of this man were true
paraphrase: Many people came to Jesus and observed that although John performed no miracle, everything he had said about Jesus was true.
contexte: After escaping arrest in Jerusalem, Jesus withdrew beyond Jordan to the place where John first baptized, and many came to him there.

citation: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
paraphrase: Jesus, deeply troubled, solemnly declares that one of his disciples will betray him.
contexte: After washing the disciples' feet and predicting his betrayal, Jesus is troubled in spirit and testifies that one of his disciples will betray him.

citation: I am the way, the truth, and the life
paraphrase: Jesus declares that he himself is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one can come to the Father except through him.
contexte: Thomas has just asked Jesus how the disciples can know the way to where he is going.

citation: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive
paraphrase: Jesus identifies the promised Comforter as the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot accept because it neither sees nor knows Him, but the disciples know Him because He dwells with them and will be in them.
contexte: During the Last Supper discourse, Jesus promises to ask the Father to send another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, to abide with His disciples forever.

citation: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples, using the metaphor of the vine and branches to illustrate their relationship and the importance of bearing fruit.

citation: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
paraphrase: When the Comforter comes, whom I will send from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples about the coming of the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, after addressing the world's hatred.

citation: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
paraphrase: Jesus tells his disciples that despite their sorrow, he must leave because it is beneficial for them; otherwise the Comforter (Holy Spirit) cannot come, but if he goes, he will send him.
contexte: Jesus is speaking to his disciples about his impending departure, which has filled their hearts with sorrow.

citation: the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth
paraphrase: Jesus explains that when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide the disciples into all truth, speaking only what He hears and revealing future events.
contexte: Jesus is preparing his disciples for his departure, explaining that the Holy Spirit will come to guide them into all truth, since they cannot yet bear everything he has to say.

citation: that they might know thee the only true God
paraphrase: Eternal life consists in knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent.
contexte: In his prayer to the Father, Jesus asks to be glorified so that he may give eternal life to those given to him.

citation: and have known surely that I came out from thee
paraphrase: Jesus tells the Father that he has passed on the words the Father gave him, and the disciples received them, truly knowing that Jesus came from the Father and believing that the Father sent him.
contexte: In his prayer to the Father, Jesus speaks about the disciples whom the Father gave him and who have accepted his teaching.

citation: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
contexte: Jesus is praying to the Father for his disciples, asking that they be kept from evil and sanctified as they are sent into the world.

citation: I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth
paraphrase: Jesus consecrates himself for his disciples' sake so that they too may be truly sanctified.
contexte: In his prayer to the Father, Jesus asks that his disciples be sanctified by the truth and then consecrates himself on their behalf.

citation: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.
paraphrase: Jesus affirms that his birth and coming into the world were for the purpose of bearing witness to the truth, and that everyone who belongs to the truth listens to his voice.
contexte: During Jesus' trial before Pilate, after Jesus has explained that his kingdom is not of this world, Pilate asks him if he is a king.

citation: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth?
paraphrase: Pilate asks Jesus what truth is, then goes out to the Jews and says he finds no fault in Jesus.
contexte: After Jesus speaks of bearing witness to the truth, Pilate asks his famous question and then declares Jesus innocent to the Jews.

citation: And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true
paraphrase: The eyewitness testifies truthfully, knowing his testimony is true, so that you may believe.
contexte: After a soldier pierced Jesus' side, an eyewitness testifies to what happened so that readers may believe.

citation: and we know that his testimony is true.
paraphrase: The disciple who testifies and wrote these things is the one mentioned, and we know his testimony is true.
contexte: After Jesus's remarks about the beloved disciple's future, the narrator identifies that disciple as the one who testifies and wrote these things, affirming the truth of his testimony.

citation: Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
paraphrase: Peter declares that he now truly understands that God shows no partiality, accepting people from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.
contexte: At Cornelius's house, Peter responds to Cornelius's explanation of why he sent for him, acknowledging that God had guided the meeting.

citation: wist not that it was true which was done by the angel
paraphrase: Peter followed the angel out of the prison, but he did not realize that what the angel was doing was actually happening; he thought he was seeing a vision.
contexte: Peter has been miraculously freed from prison by an angel and is following him out, but he does not yet realize the event is real.

citation: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
paraphrase: Peter, coming to his senses, declares with certainty that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued him from Herod's power and from all that the Jewish people expected.
contexte: After being miraculously freed from prison by an angel, Peter realizes he is not dreaming but has been truly delivered.

citation: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
paraphrase: Paul denies Festus's accusation of madness, asserting that he speaks words of truth and soberness.
contexte: Festus interrupts Paul's defense with a loud accusation of madness, and Paul responds respectfully, denying the charge and affirming the truth and sobriety of his words.

citation: who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
paraphrase: God's wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
contexte: Paul explains that the gospel reveals God's righteousness, while His wrath is revealed against those who suppress the truth.

citation: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
paraphrase: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served created things rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
contexte: Paul describes how humanity, having turned from God's glory to images of created things, exchanged God's truth for a lie and served the creature rather than the Creator.

citation: the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things
paraphrase: Paul affirms that God's judgment against those who practice such things is based on truth.
contexte: Paul is addressing those who judge others while committing the same sins, asserting that God's judgment is according to truth.

citation: and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
paraphrase: For those who are contentious and disobedient to the truth, choosing instead to follow unrighteousness, there will be indignation and wrath.
contexte: Paul explains that God will render to each person according to their deeds, contrasting those who patiently seek glory with those who are contentious and disobey the truth.

citation: the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law
paraphrase: You are confident that you are a guide to the blind and a teacher of the foolish, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth.
contexte: Paul addresses those who rely on the law and presume to guide others, yet fail to live up to their own teaching.

citation: let God be true, but every man a liar
paraphrase: Paul rejects the idea that human unfaithfulness can nullify God's faithfulness, affirming that God is true and every human is a liar, as Scripture says that God is justified in His words and prevails when judged.
contexte: Paul responds to the objection that Jewish unbelief might nullify God's faithfulness, arguing that God's truth remains despite human falsehood.

citation: the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory
paraphrase: Paul asks that if his falsehood causes God's truthfulness to abound even more to God's glory, why is he still condemned as a sinner?
contexte: Paul responds to a hypothetical objection that his own lie or falsehood could magnify God's truth and glory, questioning why he should still be judged as a sinner.

citation: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not,
paraphrase: Paul affirms in Christ that he is speaking truthfully, not lying, and his conscience confirms this through the Holy Spirit.
contexte: Paul expresses his deep sorrow for his fellow Israelites and his willingness to be cut off from Christ for their sake.

citation: because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith
paraphrase: Paul acknowledges that the natural branches were removed because of unbelief, while the Gentiles stand only by faith, so they should not be arrogant but rather fear.
contexte: Paul is addressing Gentile believers, warning them not to boast against the Jewish branches that were broken off due to unbelief, but to stand firm in faith with humility and fear.

citation: All things indeed are pure
paraphrase: Do not let food destroy God's work; all things are pure, but it is wrong for anyone to eat in a way that causes offense.
contexte: Paul urges believers to pursue peace and mutual edification, warning against letting dietary practices destroy God's work.

citation: Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God
paraphrase: Paul declares that Jesus Christ became a servant to the Jews to demonstrate God's truthfulness by fulfilling the promises made to the patriarchs.
contexte: Paul exhorts the Roman believers to unity and mutual acceptance, citing Christ's ministry to the circumcision as a foundation for both Jews and Gentiles to glorify God.

citation: but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth
paraphrase: Since Christ our Passover has been sacrificed, let us celebrate the festival not with the old leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
contexte: Paul instructs the Corinthian church to remove the old leaven of sin, because Christ our Passover has been sacrificed.

citation: but rejoiceth in the truth;
paraphrase: Charity does not celebrate wrongdoing but finds joy in the truth.
contexte: In a passage describing the qualities of charity, Paul contrasts its rejection of wrongdoing with its delight in the truth.

citation: But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
contexte: Paul defends his change of travel plans against accusations of fickleness, insisting his word to the Corinthians was not unreliable.

citation: But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
paraphrase: We have rejected secret and shameful ways, not walking in deceit or falsifying God's word, but by openly showing the truth we commend ourselves to everyone's conscience before God.
contexte: Paul defends his ministry, stating that he and his companions have renounced deceit and instead openly proclaim the truth.

citation: By the word of truth, by the power of God
paraphrase: Paul describes how he and his companions commend themselves as ministers of God through the message of truth, God's power, and the weapons of righteousness.
contexte: Paul lists the hardships and virtues that commend him and his fellow ministers as servants of God.

citation: as deceivers, and yet true;
paraphrase: Paul describes how he and his companions endure both honor and dishonor, evil reports and good reports, being treated as impostors yet remaining true.
contexte: Paul lists the hardships and paradoxical conditions he and his fellow workers experience while commending themselves as ministers of God.

citation: as we spake all things to you in truth
paraphrase: Paul explains that his boast about the Corinthians to Titus did not disappoint him, because just as he spoke truthfully to them, his boasting to Titus proved to be true.
contexte: Paul assures the Corinthians that his earlier boasting about them to Titus was justified, and that his truthful speech to them is confirmed by Titus's joyful experience.

citation: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me
paraphrase: Paul swears by the truth of Christ within him that no one will prevent him from boasting about his conduct in Achaia.
contexte: Paul defends his refusal to burden the Corinthians financially, contrasting his conduct with that of false apostles.

citation: I will say the truth
paraphrase: Paul says that if he boasts, he would not be foolish because he would speak the truth, but he refrains so that no one thinks more of him than what they see or hear.
contexte: Paul continues his 'foolish' boasting, explaining that even if he boasts, he will speak the truth, but he refrains to avoid giving others an exaggerated opinion of him.

citation: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
contexte: Paul is writing to the Corinthians, expressing his hope that they will do what is right and explaining that his authority is for building them up, not tearing them down.

citation: that the truth of the gospel might continue with you
paraphrase: Paul explains that he refused to submit to the false brethren for even a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with the Galatians.
contexte: Paul describes how false brethren wanted to bring them into bondage, and he says he did not yield to them even for an hour.

citation: they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel
paraphrase: When Paul saw that they were not acting consistently with the gospel's truth, he rebuked Peter in front of everyone, asking why he, a Jew who lives like a Gentile, would compel Gentiles to live like Jews.
contexte: Paul confronts Peter publicly in Antioch because Peter had withdrawn from eating with Gentiles after certain men from James arrived, and other Jews, including Barnabas, followed his dissimulation.

citation: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
contexte: Paul reminds the Galatians how they once welcomed him despite his physical affliction, yet now they treat him as an enemy for speaking the truth.

citation: who did hinder you that ye should not obey the truth?
paraphrase: Paul asks the Galatians who has hindered them, since they started well but are now not obeying the truth.
contexte: Paul is addressing the Galatian believers, reminding them of their previous faithful obedience and asking who has hindered their progress in the truth.

citation: ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation
paraphrase: In Christ you also trusted after hearing the message of truth—the gospel of your salvation—and after believing, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.
contexte: Paul explains that the Ephesian believers, after hearing the gospel, trusted in Christ and were sealed with the Holy Spirit as a guarantee of their inheritance.

citation: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him
paraphrase: Rather than being deceived, we should speak truth in love and grow up in every way into Christ, who is the head of the church.
contexte: Paul urges believers to mature in Christ, no longer being tossed about by deceitful doctrines, but instead speaking the truth in love so the body of Christ may grow.

citation: as the truth is in Jesus:
paraphrase: Paul reminds the Ephesians that if they have truly heard and been taught in Christ, they have come to know the truth that is in Jesus.
contexte: Paul contrasts the Gentiles' hardened, licentious behavior with what the Ephesians learned when they heard and were taught in Christ.

citation: And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.
paraphrase: Put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
contexte: Paul instructs believers to discard their old sinful nature and adopt a new nature renewed by the Spirit.

citation: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour
paraphrase: Therefore, stop lying and let each of you speak truthfully to your neighbor, because we belong to one another as members of the same body.
contexte: Paul urges believers, having put on the new man created in righteousness and true holiness, to live accordingly in the community.

citation: the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth
paraphrase: The fruit of the Spirit consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth.
contexte: Paul encourages believers to walk as children of light, having been darkness but now light in the Lord, and to prove what is acceptable to the Lord.

citation: having your loins girt about with truth
paraphrase: Stand firm, therefore, with truth fastened around your waist like a belt, and with righteousness worn as a breastplate.
contexte: Paul exhorts believers to stand firm by putting on the whole armour of God in the face of spiritual warfare.

citation: whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached
paraphrase: Paul asks what it matters that Christ is proclaimed, whether from false motives or true, and he rejoices in that fact.
contexte: Paul contrasts those who preach Christ out of contention and insincerity with those who preach out of love, and he declares that he rejoices regardless of the motive.

citation: whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just
paraphrase: Paul calls the believers to dwell on whatever is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, and admirable—anything virtuous or praiseworthy.
contexte: Paul concludes his exhortations to the Philippians, urging them to focus their thoughts on virtuous things after encouraging them to pray with thanksgiving and promising God's peace.

citation: the word of the truth of the gospel;
paraphrase: Paul is grateful for the Colossians because of the hope reserved for them in heaven, which they had previously heard about through the message of truth, the gospel.
contexte: Paul gives thanks to God for the Colossians' faith and love, which stem from the hope stored up for them in heaven, heard in the word of truth.

citation: and knew the grace of God in truth:
paraphrase: The gospel has reached the Colossians and is spreading and bearing fruit throughout the world, just as it has among them since the day they heard and truly understood God's grace.
contexte: Paul gives thanks for the Colossians' faith and love, which stem from the hope they heard in the true gospel that is now bearing fruit among them.

citation: as it is in truth, the word of God
paraphrase: Paul continually thanks God that when the Thessalonians heard his preaching, they accepted it not as merely human words but as the genuine word of God, which actively works in those who believe.
contexte: Paul gives thanks to God because the Thessalonians received the gospel he preached not as human words but as the true word of God.

citation: because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved
paraphrase: The lawless one will come with deceptive unrighteousness to those who are perishing because they did not welcome the love of the truth so as to be saved.
contexte: Paul explains that the Wicked one will deceive those who perish because they rejected the love of the truth, leading to God sending them a strong delusion.

citation: who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
paraphrase: God will condemn all who refuse to believe the truth and instead take pleasure in unrighteousness.
contexte: Paul explains that those who reject the love of the truth will be sent a strong delusion and ultimately condemned for taking pleasure in unrighteousness.

citation: through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:
paraphrase: Paul gives thanks because God chose the Thessalonians from the beginning for salvation through the Spirit's sanctification and their belief in the truth.
contexte: Paul contrasts the doomed who reject the truth with the Thessalonians, whom God chose for salvation through the Spirit's sanctification and belief in the truth.

citation: Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.
paraphrase: God our Savior desires that all people be saved and come to know the truth.
contexte: Paul urges prayers for all people, including kings and those in authority, because God our Savior wants everyone to be saved and to know the truth.

citation: I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not
paraphrase: Paul asserts that he was appointed a preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles, affirming that he speaks truthfully in Christ without lying, and that his teaching is grounded in faith and truth.
contexte: Paul explains his divine appointment as a preacher and apostle to the Gentiles, following his mention of Christ Jesus as the one mediator and ransom for all.

citation: the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth
paraphrase: If I am delayed, you will know how to conduct yourself in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
contexte: Paul writes to Timothy, anticipating a possible delay in his visit, so that Timothy may know how to conduct himself in the church, which is described as the pillar and ground of the truth.

citation: them which believe and know the truth
paraphrase: These false teachers forbid marriage and command abstinence from certain foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy that in the latter times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons, forbidding marriage and demanding abstinence from foods.

citation: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God
paraphrase: La veuve véritable, qui est seule et sans soutien, met sa confiance en Dieu et persévère dans les prières jour et nuit.
contexte: Paul conseille Timothée sur le soin des veuves, exigeant qu'on honore celles qui sont vraiment dans le besoin et qui se consacrent à Dieu.

citation: destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.
paraphrase: Paul warns Timothy that corrupt-minded men who are devoid of the truth perversely argue that godliness is a way to financial gain, and he instructs him to avoid such people.
contexte: Paul describes the arrogant false teachers who cause disputes, in contrast to those who are content with godliness, urging Timothy to separate from them.

citation: Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come
paraphrase: By doing good and being generous, they store up for themselves a good foundation for the future so that they may take hold of eternal life.
contexte: Paul instructs Timothy to charge the rich to be generous and store up a good foundation for the future.

citation: rightly dividing the word of truth.
paraphrase: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God as a workman who has no need to be ashamed, accurately handling the word of truth.
contexte: Paul exhorts Timothy to remain faithful and diligent in teaching, in contrast to those who engage in useless disputes and ungodly talk.

citation: Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already
paraphrase: These men have strayed from the truth by claiming the resurrection has already happened, and they are destroying the faith of some.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about false teachers like Hymenaeus and Philetus, whose erroneous teaching spreads like gangrene.

citation: if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;
paraphrase: Correct opponents with meekness, hoping that God may grant them repentance leading to the knowledge of the truth.
contexte: Paul instructs Timothy on how a servant of the Lord should gently and patiently correct those who oppose the truth.

citation: never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
paraphrase: Paul warns that false teachers are constantly learning but can never arrive at a genuine knowledge of the truth.
contexte: Paul describes the corrupt character of false teachers who oppose the truth despite their constant learning.

citation: so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds
paraphrase: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these false teachers likewise resist the truth, being men with corrupted minds and disqualified regarding the faith.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy about deceivers who, like the magicians Jannes and Jambres who opposed Moses, resist the truth and have corrupted minds.

citation: And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.
paraphrase: People will refuse to listen to the truth and will instead turn to myths.
contexte: Paul warns Timothy that people will reject sound doctrine and instead follow their own desires, turning from truth to myths.

citation: the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness
paraphrase: Paul, a servant of God and apostle of Jesus Christ, writes in accord with the faith of God's chosen people and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness.
contexte: Paul opens his letter to Titus by identifying himself as a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, writing in hope of eternal life promised by God.

citation: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught
paraphrase: A bishop must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as it has been taught, so that he can encourage others by sound doctrine and refute those who oppose it.
contexte: Paul instructs Titus on the qualifications of bishops, emphasizing that they must hold firmly to the trustworthy word so they can encourage others and refute those who oppose sound doctrine.

citation: This witness is true.
paraphrase: Paul affirms that the testimony about the Cretans is true, so Titus should rebuke them sharply so they may become sound in the faith.
contexte: Paul cites a Cretan prophet's testimony about the Cretans' character to instruct Titus to rebuke false teachers sharply.

citation: Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.
paraphrase: Instead of paying attention to Jewish myths and human rules, which cause people to turn away from the truth.
contexte: Paul instructs Titus to rebuke the Cretan believers sharply so they may be sound in the faith and not pay attention to Jewish myths and human commands.

citation: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
paraphrase: Christ serves as a minister in the heavenly sanctuary, the genuine tabernacle that the Lord established rather than any human-made structure.
contexte: Having summarized that believers have a high priest seated at God's right hand in heaven, the author now describes that priest as a minister of the true tabernacle.

citation: the figures of the true; but into heaven itself
paraphrase: Christ did not enter an earthly sanctuary that merely copies the true one, but entered heaven itself to appear before God on our behalf.
contexte: The author contrasts the earthly tabernacle's repeated sacrifices with Christ's once-for-all entrance into heaven itself.

citation: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith
paraphrase: Because Jesus has opened the way, we should approach God with sincere hearts and complete confidence in our faith, our consciences cleansed from guilt and our bodies washed with pure water.
contexte: After describing Jesus as our high priest who opened a new and living way through his flesh, the author urges believers to approach God sincerely and confidently.

citation: after that we have received the knowledge of the truth
paraphrase: If we deliberately continue sinning after knowing the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains.
contexte: Following exhortations to persevere in faith and community, the author warns against deliberate sin after receiving the truth.

citation: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth
paraphrase: God chose of his own will to give us spiritual birth through the message of truth, so that we might be a firstfruits among his creation.
contexte: James contrasts the unchanging goodness of God, the Father of lights, with the error of being deceived, showing that God voluntarily brought believers forth by the message of truth.

citation: glory not, and lie not against the truth
paraphrase: If you harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast about it or deny the truth.
contexte: James contrasts true wisdom from above with earthly wisdom that produces envy and strife, warning against lying against the truth.

citation: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;
contexte: After using Elijah as an example of effective prayer, James addresses the community about restoring those who wander from the truth.

citation: ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit
paraphrase: Since you have purified your souls by obeying the truth through the Spirit, resulting in sincere love for fellow believers, love one another deeply with a pure heart.
contexte: After speaking of Christ's foreordination and the believers' faith and hope in God through Him, Peter now calls them to live out that faith by purifying their souls through obedience to the truth and loving one another fervently.

citation: this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand
paraphrase: I have written briefly through Silvanus, a faithful brother, to encourage you and testify that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.
contexte: Peter concludes his letter by mentioning Silvanus, greeting the church, and affirming the true grace of God.

citation: established in the present truth
paraphrase: Peter affirms he will diligently remind believers of these truths, even though they already know them and are firmly grounded in the truth they presently possess.
contexte: Peter, knowing his death is near, urges believers to remember the truths they already know and to remain established in them.

citation: the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.
paraphrase: Many people will follow the destructive practices of false teachers, and because of these followers, the true way of God will be slandered.
contexte: Peter warns that false teachers will arise and many will follow their destructive ways, causing the truth to be blasphemed.

citation: according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again
paraphrase: The apostates' relapse into sin confirms the truth of the proverb that a dog returns to its own vomit and a washed sow goes back to wallowing in the mire.
contexte: Peter warns that false teachers who have known Christ but returned to sin end up worse than before, their relapse illustrating a well-known proverb.

citation: we lie, and do not the truth
paraphrase: If we claim to have fellowship with God yet continue to walk in darkness, we are lying and not living out the truth.
contexte: John is contrasting the claim of fellowship with God against the reality of walking in darkness, building on the message that God is light.

citation: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
paraphrase: If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
contexte: John is contrasting those who claim sinlessness with those who walk in the light, emphasizing that denying our sin is self-deception and contradicts the truth.

citation: and the truth is not in him.
paraphrase: Anyone who claims to know God but does not obey His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
contexte: John contrasts those who claim to know God while disobeying His commandments with those who truly know Him by keeping His word.

citation: which thing is true in him and in you
paraphrase: John reaffirms the commandment to walk as Christ walked, asserting that this truth is realized both in Christ and in the believers, since the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
contexte: John contrasts the old commandment heard from the beginning with a new commandment now fully realized in Christ and in believers, as darkness gives way to the true light.

citation: but because ye know it, and that no lie is of the truth
paraphrase: I did not write to you because you are ignorant of the truth, but because you know it, and you know that no lie belongs to the truth.
contexte: John warns his readers about those who left the church, affirming that his readers possess the truth through the Holy Spirit's anointing.

citation: and is truth, and is no lie
paraphrase: The anointing received from him remains in you, so you do not need anyone to teach you; that same anointing teaches you about all things, is true and not a lie, and just as it has taught you, remain in him.
contexte: John warns his readers about deceivers and assures them that the anointing they have received from God remains in them, teaches them all things, and is true.

citation: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
paraphrase: John exhorts his dear children not to love with empty words or talk, but with actions and in truth.
contexte: After teaching that love is shown by sacrificial action, John urges his readers to love not merely in words but in genuine deeds.

citation: And hereby we know that we are of the truth
paraphrase: By loving in deed and truth, we can know that we belong to the truth and set our hearts at rest before God.
contexte: John exhorts believers to love not merely in words but in action and truth, and explains that such genuine love gives us assurance before God.

citation: Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
paraphrase: We belong to God; those who know God listen to us, while those who do not belong to God do not listen to us. This is how we recognize the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.
contexte: John contrasts the world's reception of false teachers with the church's reception of God's messengers, providing a test for distinguishing the Spirit of truth from the spirit of error.

citation: And it is the Spirit that beareth witness, because the Spirit is truth.
paraphrase: Jesus Christ is the one who came by water and blood, not by water only but by water and blood; and the Spirit testifies to this, because the Spirit is truth.
contexte: Having stated that faith in Jesus as the Son of God overcomes the world, John now testifies that Jesus came by water and blood and that the Spirit, who is truth, bears witness.

citation: that we may know him that is true
paraphrase: We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true God; we are in the true God through his Son Jesus Christ, who is the true God and eternal life.
contexte: John concludes his letter by assuring believers that they have true knowledge through the Son of God, in contrast to the wicked world and idols.

citation: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
paraphrase: The elder sends greetings to the chosen lady and her children, loving them in the truth, and not only he but also all who have known the truth.
contexte: John, the elder, addresses the elect lady and her children, expressing love in the truth and noting that all who know the truth share this love.

citation: For the truth’s sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever.
paraphrase: Because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever, I love you.
contexte: The elder writes to the elect lady and her children, expressing his love for them in the truth and his joy that some of her children are walking in the truth.

citation: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
paraphrase: May grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, be with you in truth and love.
contexte: John greets the elect lady and her children, extending grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Jesus Christ, in truth and love.

citation: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth
paraphrase: I was overjoyed to discover that some of your children are living according to the truth, just as the Father commanded us.
contexte: John writes to the elect lady and her children, expressing joy that some of her children are walking in the truth, in line with the commandment from the Father.

citation: whom I love in the truth
paraphrase: The elder writes to the beloved Gaius, whom he loves in the truth.
contexte: The elder John addresses his beloved Gaius, expressing his love in the truth and wishing him prosperity and health.

citation: the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth
paraphrase: John rejoiced greatly when brethren came and testified to the truth that is in Gaius, just as he walks in the truth.
contexte: The elder John writes to his beloved Gaius, expressing joy upon hearing from brethren that Gaius walks in the truth.

citation: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
contexte: The elder expresses his joy over Gaius and the brethren who testify to the truth in him and walk in it.

citation: that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth
paraphrase: We should welcome and support such faithful workers so that we may become co-workers with the truth.
contexte: John encourages the church to support traveling missionaries who have gone out for the sake of Christ, so that believers may work together for the truth.

citation: and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record
paraphrase: Demetrius is well spoken of by everyone, and by the truth itself; we also testify to this, and you know our testimony is true.
contexte: After warning about the wicked deeds of Diotrephes, the elder contrasts him with Demetrius, whose good character is affirmed by all and by the truth itself.

citation: he that is holy, he that is true
paraphrase: Christ, addressing the church in Philadelphia, identifies himself as holy and true, possessing the key of David with absolute authority to open and shut, demonstrating his sovereignty and truthfulness.
contexte: Jesus instructs John to write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia, introducing himself with divine attributes.

citation: These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness
paraphrase: Jesus, the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the origin of God's creation, commands John to write to the angel of the church of Laodicea.
contexte: Christ dictates a message to the angel of the church in Laodicea, following a call for all churches to hear what the Spirit says.

citation: O Lord, holy and true
paraphrase: The martyred souls cry out to God, calling Him holy and true, asking how long until He judges and avenges their blood on those who dwell on the earth.
contexte: Under the fifth seal, the souls of those slain for the word of God cry out to God for justice.

citation: just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.
paraphrase: The victorious saints sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God for His great and marvelous works, and declaring His ways just and true, acknowledging Him as King of saints.
contexte: The redeemed stand on a sea of glass and sing a song of praise to God for His great and marvelous works, acknowledging His just and true ways.

citation: true and righteous are thy judgments
paraphrase: John heard a voice from the altar saying that the Lord God Almighty's judgments are true and righteous.
contexte: During the pouring out of the vials of God's wrath, a voice from the altar affirms the justice of God's judgments.

citation: For true and righteous are his judgments
paraphrase: His judgments are true and righteous, for He has judged the great whore who corrupted the earth, and He has avenged the blood of His servants.
contexte: A great multitude in heaven praises God for His true and righteous judgments.

citation: These are the true sayings of God.
paraphrase: The angel tells John to write that those called to the marriage supper of the Lamb are blessed, and declares that these words are the true sayings of God.
contexte: An angel instructs John to write a blessing on those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb, affirming the truth of God's words.

citation: was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge
paraphrase: John witnesses heaven opening and a white horse appearing; its rider is called Faithful and True, and he judges and wages war in righteousness.
contexte: After an angel tells John to write that the marriage supper of the Lamb is blessed and that these are the true sayings of God, John sees heaven open and a white horse whose rider is named Faithful and True.

citation: for these words are true and faithful
paraphrase: The one seated on the throne declares that he is making all things new and instructs John to write, because these words are true and faithful.
contexte: God, seated on the throne, announces the renewal of all things and commands John to write, affirming the truth and faithfulness of these words.

citation: These sayings are faithful and true
paraphrase: An angel tells John that these words are faithful and true, and that the God of the prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place.
contexte: After describing the eternal city where God's servants will reign forever, an angel speaks to John about the truth of the revelation.
